findings.location: "html > body > main > form > button", <button> button, text 'Submit', line 36
findings.violation: The form's primary button is labelled Submit, a generic word that says nothing about what pressing it does.

findings.fix: Remove the confirmation field and offer a control that shows the password as typed.
findings.violation: The form asks for the new password a second time to confirm it, doubling the typing for every person.

findings.evidence: <input id="email" name="email" type="text" autocomplete="email" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" autocapitalize="none" required>
findings.violation: This email field is type text, so a phone does not show the keyboard built for it.

findings.fix: Offer the options as visible radio buttons.
findings.violation: A single choice among 3 options sits in a drop-down, so the person must open it to see them.

findings.evidence: <input id="password" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" minlength="6" required>

note: golden-01.html is a club sign-up form that plants five single-occurrence defects, each graded at severity 2 because each adds work without blocking completion. The email field declares the text type, so a phone opens the full keyboard (FORMS-INPUT-TYPE, one field, so the lesser recurrence grade). The squad choice offers three real options in a drop-down, not counting its empty-valued prompt (FORMS-OPTION-CONTROL). The new password allows six characters, below the eight the operational test sets (FORMS-PASSWORD-RULES, the minlength branch). A Confirm password field repeats it (FORMS-CONFIRM-PASSWORD, fixed at 2). The only button reads Submit (FORMS-ACTION-LABEL, fixed at 2). Every other field carries its autofill token and switches autocorrect off, so no other criterion fires.
